source_text:
Περὶ δὲ Φίλωνος τοῦ διακόνου ἀπὸ Κιλικίας, ἀνδρὸς μεμαρτυρημένου, ὃς καὶ νῦν ἐν λόγῳ θεοῦ ὑπηρετεῖ μοι ἅμα Ῥέῳ Ἀγαθόποδι, ἀνδρὶ ἐκλεκτῷ, ὃς ἀπὸ Συρίας μοι ἀκολουθεῖ ἀποταξάμενος τῷ βίῳ, οἳ καὶ μαρτυροῦσιν ὑμῖν, κἀγὼ τῷ θεῷ εὐχαριστῶ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἐδέξασθε αὐτούς, ὡς καὶ ὑμᾶς ὁ κύριος: οἱ δὲ ἀτιμάσαντες αὐτοὺς λυτρωθείησαν ἐν τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἡ ἀγάπη τῶν ἀδελφῶν τῶν ἐν Τρωάδι: ὅθεν καὶ γράφω ὑμῖν διὰ Βούρρου πεμφθέντος ἄμα ἐμοὶ ἀπὸ Ἐφεσίων καὶ Σμυρναίων εἰς λόγον τιμῆς. τιμήσει αὐτοὺς ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, εἰς ὃν ἐλπίζουσιν σαρκί, ψυχῇ, πνεύματι, πίστει, ἀγάπῃ, ὁμονοίᾳ, ἔρρωσθε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, τῇ κοινῇ ἐλπίδι ἡμῶν.
thought_title: Commendation of Philo and Rheus Agathopus, and greetings from Troas
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Smyrnaeans, commending two companions who have served him and sending greetings from the brothers in Troas.
pass_a_gloss: Now concerning Philo the deacon from Cilicia, a man having been witnessed to, who also now in word of God serves me together with Rheus Agathopus, a man chosen, who from Syria follows me having renounced the life, who also bear witness to you, and I to God give thanks on behalf of you, because you received them, as also you the Lord: but the ones having dishonored them may they be redeemed in the grace of Jesus Christ. Greets you the love of the brothers of the ones in Troas: from where also I write to you through Burrhus having been sent together with me from Ephesians and Smyrnaeans for word of honor. Will honor them the Lord Jesus Christ, in whom they hope in flesh, in soul, in spirit, in faith, in love, in concord. Farewell in Christ Jesus, in the common hope of us.

lemmas.gloss: having renounced, having bid farewell to
the life, former way of life
having dishonored, having treated with contempt

choices.why: The perfect passive participle carries the sense of a reputation established by testimony; 'attested character' conveys this without implying formal legal witness.
rejected: a man who has been witnessed

choices.why: The aorist middle participle with dative βίῳ means to bid farewell to or renounce one's former way of life; 'former' is implied by the context of following Ignatius.
The optative expresses a wish or prayer; 'redeemed' preserves the ransom metaphor of λυτρόω.
The phrase means 'for the purpose of honor' or 'as an expression of honor'; 'mark of honor' captures the intent of the sending.
The standard epistolary closing formula; 'be strong' is the literal root but 'farewell' is the conventional English equivalent for letter closings.

pass_b_english: Now about Philo, the deacon from Cilicia. He is a man of attested character, and even now he serves me in the word of God together with Rheus Agathopus, a chosen man who has followed me from Syria after renouncing his former life. Both of them bear witness to you, and I thank God on your behalf because you welcomed them as the Lord welcomed you. As for those who dishonored them, may they be redeemed in the grace of Jesus Christ.

The love of the brothers and sisters in Troas greets you. It is from there that I am writing to you through Burrhus, who was sent with me by the Ephesians and Smyrnaeans as a mark of honor. The Lord Jesus Christ will honor them, for in him they hope with flesh, soul, spirit, faith, love, and concord. Farewell in Christ Jesus, our common hope.

problems.quote: as the Lord would welcome you
problems.why: Source says 'as the Lord also welcomed you' (past tense), not a hypothetical 'would welcome you.'
problems.fix: as the Lord also welcomed you
problems.ruling: ὡς καὶ ὑμᾶς ὁ κύριος: aorist ἐδέξασθε 'received/welcomed' is past tense, not hypothetical 'would welcome.'

edits.old: as the Lord would welcome you
edits.new: as the Lord also welcomed you

problems.why: Reader may not realize 'council of elders' = 'elders' = presbyterion, and 'council of the apostles' is a typological parallel, not a different group.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note; clarify 'council of the apostles' as typology.

edits.old: as the Lord also welcomed you

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' does not appear in this passage; no change needed here.

The English 'as the Lord also welcomed you' was flagged, but the source has 'ὡς καὶ ὑμᾶς ὁ κύριος' (as also you the Lord), which the English already renders accurately with 'as the Lord also welcomed you'. No change needed.

last_rejected.why: Future indicative 'will honor' loses the jussive/optative force of the wish/prayer; this is a benediction, not prediction.
last_rejected.fix: may the Lord Jesus Christ honor them
last_rejected.ruling: τιμήσει is future indicative, not optative; 'will honor' correctly renders the form. No jussive force in source.

last_rejected.why: ἐλπίζουσιν is third person plural, but the antecedent is ambiguous; however 'they' refers to the Ephesians and Smyrnaeans (who sent Burrhus), not 'them' (Philo and Rheus Agathopus). The English 'they' is unclear but grammatically points to nearest plural 'them' (the honored ones).
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς ὃν ἐλπίζουσιν: 'they' is grammatical; antecedent ambiguity exists in Greek itself, not a translation error.

last_rejected.why: English omits the dative 'in' or 'with'—the farewell is 'Farewell in Christ Jesus, [in] our common hope', not a mere apposition.
last_rejected.fix: Farewell in Christ Jesus, in our common hope
last_rejected.ruling: τῇ κοινῇ ἐλπίδι ἡμῶν as apposition to Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ is a valid rendering of the dative; no meaning lost.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening transition, separated the greeting from the writing note, and made the pronoun references and sentence flow more natural for modern readers.

notes.why: The name appears as 'Rheus Agathopus' (full name) and likely 'Agathopus' alone; but also check if 'Rheus' is a separate name or title. Actually in 6.10 it's 'Rheus Agathopus' again. No drift found—false flag.

facts: Rheus Agathopus is otherwise unknown; he appears only in Ignatius's letters as a companion.
notes.why: No identification is given; reader may wonder if he is a known figure.
notes.fix: Note that he is otherwise unknown.
